simulation.setup: 30 simulated learners x 150 practice steps, NaCCA B1-B6 graph

v2.setup: 30 simulated learners per profile and policy (seeds 0 to 29), 150 practice steps at 5 a day, then 30 days without practice; goal runs stop at 300 steps

assumptions.text: Each simulated pupil has a hidden true state for every skill. One practice step on a skill the pupil does not know teaches it with probability 0.35 when every prerequisite is truly known and 0.03 otherwise. A known skill is answered wrongly 10% of the time and an unknown one is guessed right 20% of the time. The pupil does 5 steps a day. Each night every known skill can be forgotten: a skill with memory strength S days survives one day with probability exp(-1/S). S is 45 days for a skill just learned and 365 days for what the pupil knew at the start; practising a known skill again on a later day doubles S, up to 365 days. Practising a skill does not refresh its prerequisites. These are modelling assumptions, not measurements of Ghanaian pupils.

profiles.beginner_p1: ASSUMPTION, not data. A pupil starting Basic 1: knows 15% of the B1 and B2 skills (from home and kindergarten) and 3% of everything later. Same as the v1.0 profile.
profiles.gapped_p4: ASSUMPTION, not data. A Basic 4 pupil with foundational gaps: knows 75% of the B1 to B3 skills, so one lower-primary skill in four is missing, and 5% of B4 to B6. Same as the v1.0 profile.
profiles.gapped_p6: ASSUMPTION, not data. A Basic 6 pupil with gaps that grew over the years: knows 80% of B1 to B3, 50% of B4 and B5, and 5% of B6.
profiles.uneven_strands: ASSUMPTION, not data. A Basic 4 pupil who is strong in Number and weak in Geometry and Measurement: of the B1 to B4 skills, knows 85% in Number, 15% in Geometry and Measurement and 50% in Algebra and Data; knows 5% of B5 and B6 in every strand.

policies.kwan-strict: Kwan with the library defaults (strict goal mode, no exploration, variety 0.05, review slot on). The pupil gets a list of 3 skills, practises each once in the order given, then gets a new list.
policies.kwan-explore: The same as kwan-strict with exploration switched on (eps 0.05, as in the demo).
policies.kwan-top1: Kwan used as in the v1.0 simulator, added as a sensitivity check: the pupil practises only the top pick and asks again after every answer. With a list of 1 there is no review slot.
policies.syllabus: Syllabus order from Basic 1: always the first skill, by class and then by code, that the learner model does not count as mastered. It does not use the prerequisite map.
policies.random: A skill drawn at random from the whole curriculum at every step.
policies.remedial-first: The pupil's class syllabus with remediation first: take the first skill of the pupil's class (then later classes, then earlier ones) that is not mastered; if any skill that leads to it is below 70%, practise the earliest such skill, otherwise practise the skill itself. It uses the prerequisite map but none of Kwan's scoring. With a goal, the goal is the skill it works towards.

kt_deep.task: PRD 5.6 and 5.7: deep knowledge tracing (pyKT) against elo-multi on the same folds
kt_deep.implementation: Real pyKT model classes (DKT, SAKT, simpleKT, AKT), built by pykt.models.init_model with pyKT default hyperparameters and fed by pyKT's KTDataset; not re-implementations. On CPU or CUDA they are trained by pyKT's own train_model. On Apple MPS, which has no float64, they are trained by Kwan's float32 copy of that loop (same loss, model selection and early stopping). The trainer used is recorded per model under datasets.<name>.models.<model>.trainer.

protocol.split: 5 folds by student, seed 42; each fold is held out once and no student is in two folds
protocol.validation: 10% of each fold's training students (seed 42 + fold) are used only to pick the best epoch of the deep models; the held-out fold is never used for model selection
protocol.sequence_format: pyKT: each student's answers are cut into pieces of at most 200, padded with -1; a last piece shorter than 3 answers is dropped; a deep model sees one piece at a time
protocol.scored_answers: every answer of a held-out sequence except its first (pyKT's next-answer scoring); elo-multi is scored on exactly these answers, after reading each held-out student's full history in order
protocol.elo_multi: kwan.eval.kt.Elo2: item difficulty fitted on the training students (two passes), held-out students predicted online
protocol.metrics: AUC, RMSE, accuracy at 0.5; mean and sample standard deviation (n - 1) across folds

budget.pykt_reference_budget: 200 epochs with early stopping (patience 10) on a GPU
budget.note: Reduced budget: every fit was capped at far fewer epochs than pyKT's reference runs. Where a fit was stopped by the cap, the model's AUC is likely below what full training would reach. The cap, the epochs run and the count of folds stopped by the cap are under datasets.<name>.models.<model>. train_minutes_total adds up fits that ran side by side on one shared GPU.

latency_protocol.clock: ms_per_update_cpu is process CPU time, so that other work on a shared machine does not inflate it; ms_per_update_wall is the wall-time median of the same passes
latency_protocol.deep_models: one forward pass for one learner over a full window (199 past answers plus the item to predict), batch size 1, CPU, 1 thread, no gradients; median of 200 timed passes after 20 warm-up passes
latency_protocol.elo_multi: one prediction and one update per answer, pure Python, 1 thread: CPU time of a pass over up to 50,000 held-out answers of fold 0 divided by their number; median of 5 passes
latency_protocol.note: The deep figure is the most favourable serving case: one next-answer prediction. Kwan needs mastery for every candidate skill after each answer, which costs the attention models one pass per candidate.

decision.rule: D7: a deep model is adopted only if it beats elo-multi by at least 0.03 AUC on at least two of AMMORE, Eedi and ASSISTments 2009, and stays under 20 ms per update on CPU.
decision.reason: No deep model meets rule D7. The closest is simplekt: at least 0.03 AUC ahead of elo-multi (Kwan) on 0 of the 3 D7 datasets it was run on (needs 2); its best margin is +0.0089 on eedi_34. Elo stays the only learner model.

shipped.rule: tau: the value with the best mean validation AUC at the v1 step sizes on eedi_2020_task34, eedi_2020_task12; k_s, k_k, decay: the triple with the best mean validation AUC across assistments_2009, eedi_2020_task34, eedi_2020_task12 at that tau; then never worse than the v1 defaults by more than 0.002 AUC on the held-out students of assistments_2009, eedi_2020_task34 (a parameter that breaks this goes back to its v1 value); grade_step and transfer keep the v1 values because the public datasets have no prerequisite graph; streak_to_master and streak_expiry_days are not fitted (PRD defaults)

acceptance.rule: forgetting never lowers AUC by more than 0.002 on datasets without timestamps

notes: grade_step and transfer act only through a prerequisite graph; the public datasets have none, so they keep the v1 values
the grid's banks are fitted on the inner fit students; the saved banks on all the training students
